reconcile.connective: The leading harmonization restricts "everlasting" to the covenant of grace, not to circumcision itself, so the rite could lapse in Christ without breaking Genesis 17's promise.

discrepancy.connective: The sharpest objection is pressed by Steven DiMattei, who argues the Priestly writer's "eternal covenant" of circumcision in Genesis 17 is flatly subverted by Paul, who cherry-picks the earlier uncircumcised-Abraham account to make the rite optional.

skeptic.name: Steven DiMattei
skeptic.work: Contradictions in the Bible (contradictionsinthebible.com), "#31. Is the covenant of circumcision an eternal covenant OR not?"
skeptic.attribution: Steven DiMattei, PhD, Contradictions in the Bible (#31, 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Eternal duration was promised only to the covenant established by God with the seed of Abraham, which was to grow into a multitude of nations, but not to the covenant institution which God established in connection with the lineal posterity of Abraham, the twelve tribes of Israel. … So again it was only in its essence that circumcision could be a sign of the eternal covenant.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the 'everlasting command' objection: K&D restrict the eternity of the covenant to the grace-promise to the spiritual seed, denying it ever attached to the temporary institution/sign of circumcision — so the rite's abolition in Christ does not falsify Gen 17's 'everlasting covenant.'

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on Genesis 17:15-21
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Argues the 'everlasting covenant' was promised only to the covenant of grace expanding to Abraham's spiritual seed, not to the temporary institution and sign of circumcision — the strongest PD answer on the row to the 'everlasting command' wording. (Haley's coverage of this exact pair could not be confirmed, so a row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage is used per spec.)

link.title: GotQuestions: What does it mean that neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything (Galatians 5:6)?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment: argues physical circumcision was fulfilled and internalized (circumcision of the heart) under the New Covenant rather than abolished, so Genesis 17 and Galatians 5 stand together.
